title: Trump Rails Against Fed Rate Increase, Details Pre-Vote Talk with Chair Warsh
snippet: President Donald Trump lashed out at the Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates, revealing he told Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to 'vote with the board' prior to the unanimous vote.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump sharply criticized the Federal Reserve on Wednesday following its decision to raise interest rates, revealing that he had spoken directly with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh prior to the vote. Trump voiced frustration with the central bank's direction, arguing that borrowing costs in the United States should be slashed dramatically.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted unanimously on Wednesday to lift the benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points—marking the central bank's first rate increase in three years and the first under Warsh's leadership. The Fed also signaled that another rate hike could occur before the end of the year as policymakers work to tame persistent inflationary pressures.

Tensions over Central Bank Independence

Speaking to reporters Wednesday evening, Trump disclosed details of his private conversation with Warsh ahead of the announcement. "I talked to Kevin and I said, ‘you might as well vote with the board because it's not going to matter,’" Trump said. While expressing continued personal confidence in Warsh, the president called the rest of the FOMC "a bunch of politicians" and claimed the chairman is dealing with a "very tough board."

Trump, who has long advocated for interest rates to drop to 1% or lower to boost trade and economic activity, had previously taken to social media to demand swift rate cuts. White House officials echoed his disappointment, with Senior Deputy Press Secretary Kush Desai calling the central bank's move an "unfortunate decision" that lacked a "compelling economic case."

For his part, Warsh maintained a strict stance on institutional independence during a post-decision press briefing. When asked about presidential communications, Warsh declined to elaborate, telling reporters, "I've got nothing for you on a discussion with the president." Warsh added that central bank independence is a "two-way street," emphasizing that the Fed must stay in its lane regarding monetary policy while allowing elected leaders to manage trade and fiscal policy.

Political Crossfire

The rate hike quickly drew reactions from Capitol Hill, where Congressional Democrats pushed back against the administration's narrative, framing the rate increase as a direct consequence of Trump's own economic policies.

Rep. Brendan Boyle (D-PA), the ranking member of the House Budget Committee, stated that the interest rate hike proves the administration's economic agenda is failing American consumers. Meanwhile, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) argued that the Fed would likely be contemplating rate cuts if not for the inflationary fallout caused by Trump's policy decisions.
